title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows: shared meeting timer from the room console
summary: The roadmap description, Pro entitlement and published Pro price are supported, and searches confirmed the gaps in timer-specific controls and rollout guidance. The cost rating conflicts with the page's stated licensing expenditure, and January's roadmap target is incorrectly described as the earliest possible availability.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The countdown may appear from January CY2027 at the earliest.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Windows shared countdown meeting timer admin setting default version rollout roles audit logs licensing; "Teams Rooms" "meeting timer". Roadmap gives only a January CY2027 target; no source establishes the earliest possible availability.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: Tell room owners and meeting organisers that a shared countdown on the front-of-room display and in participants' meeting views is targeted for January CY2027 on the roadmap, not committed for that month.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The low cost rating is consistent with the page's stated direct Pro licensing expenditure.
claims.quote: cost: "low"; 'the licence cost of moving any Basic-licensed room to Pro if you want the timer there'; 'the cost is Pro licensing for any room not already on it'. The standard defines low as indirect cost only.
claims.fix: Keep cost low but narrow the cost rationale to 'Low. For rooms already licensed with Teams Rooms Pro, the known incremental cost is admin time; no separate timer meter is documented.' In Cost and licensing, replace the last paragraph with 'Indirect cost is admin time. Moving a Basic-licensed room to Pro would be a separate licensing purchase; Microsoft lists Pro starting at $40.00 room/month, paid yearly.' This separates the existing-license feature cost from the optional product upgrade.
